newsitem.title: UK: Carlton lifts H1 profits 11 percent.
newsitem.headline: Carlton lifts H1 profits 11 percent.

text.p: British broadcaster Carlton Communications Plc on Wednesday reported an 11 percent rise in half-year, pre-tax profits, partly boosted by strong growth in advertising revenue.
Carlton raised pre-tax profits to 158.6 million pounds ($262.5 million) from 143.3 million after a one-off loss of around 4.0 million pounds, in line with analyst expectations.
The half-year dividend rose 12 percent to 4.9 pence.
"Over the last three years we have consistently invested in our businesses," said chairman Michael Green in the results statement.

"We have maintained our clear focus, built up our market leading positions and enhanced both our profitability and our prospects for future growth," he noted, adding the group would build on this approach.

Carlton, which operates ITV commercial television licences for London weekday television, the English Midlands and the west of England, said its video division made a slow start to the year because of the timing of releases and variations in the mix of the business.
But the company, whose library now boasts over 7,500 hours of television programmes including almost 1,000 films, said it was optimistic about making progress in the second half.
Its Technicolor film processing operations was performing well and sales of the company's tapeless editing and broadcasting sustems was fulfilling expectations of rapid growth, the company said.
Analysts are awaiting news on whether Carlton and its partners in British Digital Broadcasting (BDB) have been awarded key digital terrestrial TV licences in Britain.
Carlton in January joined rival TV giant Granada Group Plc and Rupert Murdoch's dominant pay-per-view broadcaster British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc to form the formidable BDB.

BDB wants to offer some 15 subscription channels. The group faces competition from Digital Television Network (DTN), owned by Nasdaq-listed NTL Inc -- but in what has been dubbed a classic case of David versus Goliath, most analysts tip BDB as the winner.
Carlton, which has a cash pile of 166 million pounds, said it expected the Independent Television Commission watchdog to award the licence by the end of June.
"Digital terrestrial television brings enormous opportunities to Carlton," chairman Green stated.
